page_description: How you sign in, and what your team sees.
profile_description: Your name shows to your team. Your email is how you sign in; it can't change.
language_description: The language the admin speaks to you, on this browser.
language_not_offered: The admin doesn't have that language.
password_description: Changing it signs you out everywhere else, and ends any reset link sent before.
password_changed: Password changed. Every other device signed in to your account was signed out.
sessions_description: Where your account is signed in. Sign out a device you don't recognise, then change your password.
sessions_confirm_description: {count, plural, one {The other device} other {The # other devices}} must sign in again. This one stays signed in.
two_factor_description_on: Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
two_factor_description_off: Protect your account with a code from an authenticator app (1Password, Google Authenticator, Authy, …) as well as your password.
two_factor_password_description: To check it's you before an authenticator is added.
two_factor_scan_instructions: Scan this with your authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.
two_factor_qr_label: QR code for your authenticator app
two_factor_scan_manual: Can't scan it? Enter this key in the app instead (time-based, 6 digits):
two_factor_code_or_recovery: Code from your authenticator, or a recovery code
two_factor_regenerate_description: Your current recovery codes stop working once the new ones are made.
two_factor_disable_description: Signing in will then ask only for your password, and your recovery codes stop working.
two_factor_codes_replaced: Your old recovery codes no longer work.
two_factor_codes_keep: Keep these somewhere safe, like a password manager. Each works once to sign in without your authenticator. They won't be shown again.
two_factor_codes_file_note: Each works once, if you lose your authenticator.
